item.title: Rhode Islanders bet big on Patriots for Super Bowl, and mostly lost
item.description: CRANSTON – Rhode Islanders overwhelmingly backed the New England Patriots in Super Bowl wagering, according to post-game data from Sportsbook Rhode Island, leaving the state-run sportsbook on the winning side after the team’s loss. item.title: CVS year-end profit falls to $1.7B in 2025
item.description: WOONSOCKET – CVS Health Corp. on Tuesday reported a 2025 profit of $1.7 billion, down from the net income of $4.6 billion the company posted the previous year. item.title: Brown University increases tuition for 2026-27 academic year
item.description: PROVIDENCE – Students at Brown University will see higher tuition prices this fall, as the Ivy League school continues to grapple with a structural operating deficit and projected loss for fiscal year 2027. item.title: Woonsocket mill redevelopment adds 70 affordable housing units
item.description: WOONSOCKET – A cluster of three former mill buildings have reopened their doors as 70-units of affordable housing. Known collectively as Millrace, the buildings offer a total of six studio apartments, 57 one-bedroom units and seven two-bedroom units ranging from $749 to $1,350 in monthly rent. item.title: Castle Hill Inn plans phased reopening beginning in March
item.description: NEWPORT – The historic Castle Hill Inn has planned a phased reopening for next month following the two-alarm fire that damaged the property on Feb. 5. item.title: GA approves $18M infusion to save Roger Williams and Fatima hospitals
item.description: PROVIDENCE – The General Assembly on Tuesday unanimously approved an $18 million transfer to help close the sale of Roger Williams Medical Center and Fatima Hospital to The Centurion Foundation in time to meet a Feb. 27 deadline imposed by a federal bankruptcy court.
